callee.body_note: The callee's behavior is excluded; only its identity and extent are locked (length, SHA-256, FDE records, padding, direct call sites).
callee.direct_e8_call_sites_note: A byte-pattern scan of .text for direct e8 calls to 0x3bb2290 finds exactly three sites: this window (0x36f57d4) and two sites inside larger functions (0x36ff858, 0x3704aea). Neither of the other two sites lies inside a single-call census window (containment checked against all 31,898 census windows), so no other small single-call window calls this callee. Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and data sections are not a complete xref census.
callee.name: call-target callee (behavior excluded, bytes retained)
callee.padding_note: int3 padding to the next FDE at 0x3bb25f0; recorded exactly.

function.entry_note: The window does not start with endbr64; its first instruction is push rbx. The FDE range is the authority for the window start.
function.name: inverted-mask descriptor helper
function.padding_note: int3 padding to the next FDE at 0x36f57f0; recorded exactly.
function.prev_gap_note: int3 bytes between the previous FDE end (0x36f5782) and this window start (0x36f5790); previous function's padding, not part of this window.

incoming.direct_e8_callers_note: A byte-pattern scan of .text for direct e8 calls to 0x36f5790 finds exactly zero sites, so this packet has no caller file (five files in the work-item directory). Register-indirect references, other pointer paths, prefixes, and data sections are not a complete xref census.

rule.call: Call 0x3bb2290 with rdi = obj (unchanged input), rsi = address of the stack descriptor.

descriptor.fields: descriptor+0x00 = data pointer [rsi]; descriptor+0x08 = data+16; descriptor+0x10 = data+len+1 where len = [rsi+8]; descriptor+0x18 = mask (2 bytes); descriptor+0x20 = [rsi+0x18]
descriptor.gap_note: Descriptor bytes at +0x1a..+0x1f are not written by this window (only the 2-byte mask is stored at +0x18); the callee is assumed to read only the defined fields, and the gap is disclosed, not hidden.
descriptor.mask: mask = (~pmovmskb(data[0:16])) & 0xffff, i.e. the bitwise inversion of the 16 most-significant-bit flags of the first 16 input bytes, truncated to 16 bits (stored via dx).

mask_edges.note: Edges are model checks on the recorded arithmetic, not executions of the target binary.

rule.mask_proof: pmovmskb collects bit 7 of each of the 16 bytes into a 16-bit value; not inverts all 32 bits of edx, and storing dx keeps exactly the low 16 inverted bits. The mask is therefore the bitwise complement of the MSB pattern, independent of the remaining input bytes.
rule.return: Return obj (rbx, the unchanged first argument).
rule.summary: Derive mask = ~pmovmskb(data[0:16]) (16 bits), build a stack descriptor {data, data+16, data+len+1, mask, [rsi+0x18]}, call 0x3bb2290(obj, &descriptor), and return obj.
